summary: China's car sales fall 27% in October as EVs reach a record two-thirds of purchases, and a Reuters review finds $3 billion of data centres planned around restricted Nvidia chips.
body: Car buying in China slowed sharply in October. Retail sales of passenger cars fell 27.1% from a year earlier to 1.64 million, according to the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA), an industry group.[^1][^2] Electric and plug-in hybrid cars ("new energy vehicles") fell less, by 13.7%, so they made up a record 67.5% of all cars sold; sales of petrol-only cars almost halved.[^1] The CPCA says stricter rules for trade-in subsidies held back first-time buyers, while high fuel prices pushed people toward EVs; Just Auto points to subsidies and tax breaks withdrawn earlier this year and to rising energy costs from the Middle East war.[^1][^2]

Carmakers are making up for it abroad. Exports of electric cars rose 144.7% from a year earlier to 582,000 in October, and nearly 4.5 million have been exported so far this year.[^1] My read: this fits a pattern also seen on Singles' Day: careful shoppers at home, and companies pushing harder into foreign markets, which is why Canada, Europe and others are arguing about tariffs on Chinese EVs.

In tech, a Reuters review published Friday found more than $3 billion of Chinese computing centres planned around Nvidia chips the US has restricted, from Fujian to Inner Mongolia; documents do not show whether the chips were delivered.[^3] It comes as Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid reports linking him to a person US officials believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence. China's government calls those claims "baseless" smears.[^3][^4]
differences: US officials, as described by unnamed sources, link a former executive of the chip trader Megaspeed to Chinese intelligence; China's foreign ministry rejects this as baseless and slanderous.[^4]
